CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right ankle injury sustained during basketball

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
45-year-old male presenting with right ankle injury sustained today while playing basketball with his son at the courts. Patient reports going up for a shot when his son collided with him. Upon landing, patient twisted and rolled the ankle awkwardly. He describes pain primarily on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. Patient reports difficulty walking and sensation that the ankle feels unstable and not solid. Patient recently returned to a consistent workout routine at the gym and is concerned about disruption of his progress. He has also recently volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Focused on ankle symptoms. Denies other systemic complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not documented.

MEDICATIONS
Meloxicam (newly prescribed)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Son, age 10, actively plays basketball.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home, allowing for regular ankle elevation. Recently returned to consistent gym routine. Plays basketball recreationally with his son. Has dogs at home. Volunteering to coach basketball starting in April.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right ankle: Swelling and bruising noted on lateral side. Exquisite tenderness elicited with palpation over lateral aspect of ankle. Mild tenderness noted over medial region. Skin intact with no breakdown. Brisk capillary refill. No significant malalignment noted. Patient able to stand but unable to walk comfortably. Reports pain and instability with weight-bearing.

RESULTS
Right ankle X-rays (AP, lateral, and oblique views) demonstrate displaced lateral malleolus fracture at Weber C level. No medial or posterior malleolar fractures identified. Fracture noted to be in an unstable position.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Displaced lateral malleolar fracture of right ankle (Weber C). Surgical repair with plate and screw fixation recommended. Crutches to be provided. Meloxicam prescribed for pain and swelling management. Patient instructed to ice ankle and maintain elevation. Expected recovery time approximately 3 months. Cleared to continue coaching in April. Return to exercise and recreational activities expected after 3-month recovery period.
